title: Push API for compliance evidence, residency flags, and retention lifecycle events
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Push API (event delivery service) that emits canonical compliance events for: (1) audit/evidence bundles (evidence-ready manifests, signed URLs), (2) data residency markers when objects cross region boundaries or are served from a non-resident region, and (3) retention lifecycle transitions (scheduled deletion, retention override, retention expiration). The service must support tenant-scoped delivery policies, strong signing/authentication, at-least-once delivery with DLQ, and hooks for automatic evidence packaging on-demand.
acceptance_criteria: API supports tenant-scoped subscription configuration including event types, endpoint URL, and delivery policy (retries, backoff, DLQ).
Events emitted for audit/evidence include: event_id, tenant_id, model_version, request_id, timestamp, evidence_manifest_url (signed), residency_tags, retention_status, and schema_version.
Delivery uses per-event HMAC signatures (x-rw-signature) and optional JWT client auth; verification test vectors available in integration tests.
System guarantees at-least-once delivery and exposes a DLQ where failed events are stored for 30 days; retry/backoff configurable per-tenant.
Observability: metrics for sent/succeeded/failed retries, average time-to-first-delivery, and per-tenant delivery SLA are visible in Console dashboard.
E2E test harness that simulates slow/unavailable endpoints and validates retry/DLQ semantics is checked into infra-tests.
implementation_notes: Design: event producer publishes to internal topic (kafka) and delivery workers read, transform to canonical schema, sign, and post to tenant endpoint.
Schema: canonical event v1 with clear residency and retention enums; event.schema_version included on all events; use feature-flag for v1->v2 rollout.
Signing: HMAC-SHA256 over canonical payload. Support rotating signing keys via KMS and expose public key thumbprint for verification. Optionally support mTLS for premium tenants.
Backpressure: delivery pool per-region with token-bucket to avoid noisy neighbor; prioritize audit/evidence events over telemetry.

Evidence packaging: produce 'evidence manifest' containing stable links (pre-signed S3), hash digests, and minimal metadata to satisfy compliance exports; large bundles are referenced by manifest to avoid huge payloads. Ensure manifest URLs honor residency: if tenant requires EU-only residency, manifest links point to EU buckets.
DLQ/Retry: exponential backoff with jitter, max 20 retries over 72 hours before DLQ. Admin console can requeue DLQ items.
Testing: unit tests for signature generation/verification, integration tests with a fake endpoint server that asserts idempotency header and signature, and chaos test for broker restarts.
Observability: produce logs with delivery latency, HTTP status, body size, and last-error; expose traces with request_id and event_id for cross-service debugging.
